classification.difficultyReason: Recognise quarter, half and general sectors, distinguish a diameter from a radius, and apply the appropriate fraction of πr². Supplied angles and early working scaffolds limit interpretation.

content.prompt: Calculate the area of these parts of circles. Round to 2 d.p.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrant extending upward and rightward from a marked lower-left centre; a right-angle square and a horizontal radius labelled 2 cm.

mathematics.measurementMeaning: The labelled horizontal segment is a radius.

spec.description: Unshaded semicircle below a diameter sloping downward to the right; the midpoint is marked and the complete diameter is labelled 3.6 mm.

mathematics.measurementMeaning: The labelled segment is the diameter, so the radius is half its length.

spec.answerVisibility: The diameter is visible; its derived radius and the area are withheld.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(c), diagram above open working space
spec.description: Unshaded quadrant extending leftward and downward from a marked upper-right centre; a right-angle square and a vertical radius labelled 16 cm.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(d), diagram above open working space
spec.description: Unshaded right-hand semicircle with a vertical diameter, marked centre and a dimension arrow to the left spanning from the centre to the upper endpoint.

mathematics.measurementMeaning: The 8 m dimension spans half the diameter and therefore gives the radius.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(e), diagram above the sector-formula scaffold
spec.description: Unshaded narrow sector with its marked centre at the bottom and arc above, an interior 30° angle mark and a right radius labelled 20 mm.
spec.answerVisibility: The given interior angle and radius are visible; scaffold responses and area are withheld.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(f), diagram above open working space
spec.description: Unshaded quadrant extending leftward and downward from a marked upper-right centre, with a right-angle square and the horizontal radius labelled 2.5 cm above.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(g), diagram above open working space
spec.description: Unshaded sector extending upward and rightward from a marked lower-left centre, with a 45° interior angle mark and the lower oblique radius labelled 21.5 m.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(h), diagram above open working space
spec.description: Unshaded major sector with the omitted quarter at the lower right, a marked centre, an interior reflex angle labelled 270° and a downward radius labelled 5.1 m to its right.

mathematics.angleMeaning: The labelled 270° is inside the retained sector.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(i), diagram above open working space
spec.description: Unshaded major sector whose radii point lower left and slightly upward to the right, with a marked centre, an interior reflex angle labelled 210° and the right-hand radius labelled 36.4 km below.

mathematics.angleMeaning: The labelled 210° is inside the retained sector.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2(j), diagram above open working space
spec.description: Unshaded major sector with a narrow omitted wedge at the bottom, a marked centre, an interior reflex angle labelled 315° and a label below whose leader identifies the left oblique radius.

mathematics.angleMeaning: The labelled 315° is inside the retained sector.
mathematics.measurementMeaning: The 18.9 m leader identifies a radius, not the omitted wedge or a chord.
